# Relayium

> Relayium is an open-source, end-to-end encrypted file and online-only ephemeral text transfer tool. Its web app works on the same network and across networks (over the internet). Same-network browser sessions connect directly; cross-network browser file and text sessions carry end-to-end encrypted ciphertext through TURN by design, so the relay cannot read their content. CLI text uses a separate direct-only protocol and fails if no direct path is available. An optional stored download-link mode encrypts files in the browser (AES-256-GCM) before upload for when the recipient is offline; the server stores only ciphertext and cannot read content, filenames, or the key. Same-network transfers need no account. Creating a cross-network file or text pairing code requires sign-in, but joining with a code does not; creating a stored download link also requires the sender to sign in. Live at https://relayium.com.

## What it is

- **Category:** Secure file transfer and online-only ephemeral text transfer between devices, on the same network or across the internet.
- **Same-network (default):** Open https://relayium.com on two devices on the same network. They discover each other automatically (grouped into a "room" by shared public IP). Pick files (or drag-and-drop, up to 1,000 at once) or send an ephemeral text message; the receiver accepts the file batch and the content travels end-to-end encrypted. A text session opens straight into the composer. Comparing a short verification code is an optional extra step (advanced verification, off by default — see below). No account needed.
- **Cross-network:** two pages — realtime file and ephemeral text transfer at /cross-network (the code creator signs in; the person joining by 6-digit pairing code / join link / QR does not), and async stored file transfer at /offline-transfer (sender signs in, recipients never need an account).

## Transfer modes

- **Realtime — same network:** automatic device discovery on the LAN, direct peer-to-peer file and ephemeral text transfer over WebRTC. No account. Between two up-to-date browsers the peer card offers one action, which opens a shared workspace: one end-to-end encrypted connection carrying files and ephemeral text together, with the composer shown by default and the file and folder controls under it.
- **Realtime — pairing code (cross-network):** on the /cross-network page, a signed-in user creates a 6-digit code plus a join link and QR; the other person enters the code or opens the link without an account. The code is six decimal digits (0-9, leading zeros included) and is not the same value as the 6-digit SAS below. Codes expire 5 minutes after they are created; the countdown governs whether the code can still be used to pair, and never interrupts a transfer that is already running. Browser sessions carry end-to-end encrypted file or text ciphertext through TURN by design. Two up-to-date browsers get the same shared workspace here as on the same network — one action on the peer card, then one end-to-end encrypted connection carrying files and ephemeral text together, with one optional verification code (SAS) rather than one per session. Because that link is relayed, it also runs under a bounded lifetime derived from the TURN credential the server issued: the app warns before that boundary and ends the link at it, and a new pairing starts a new one. Peers that do not announce that exact capability — older browsers, the native apps, the CLI — keep the separate file and text flows in either room.
- **Ephemeral text:** both devices must be online at the same time. Relayium provides no offline delivery or server-side message history. Each message can contain up to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. Either endpoint can copy, log, screenshot, or otherwise retain text after receiving it. Browser text uses the WebRTC path described above; CLI text is direct-only and does not use TURN.
- **Stored download link (asynchronous):** created on the /offline-transfer page, for when the recipient is offline. A signed-in sender's browser encrypts the files before upload; the server stores only zero-knowledge ciphertext, with a settable expiry (1/3/7 days) or burn-after-first-download. Recipients need no account.
- Cross-network browser realtime transfers (a pairing code and its join link) use an encrypted TURN relay by design; the relay carries ciphertext and transport metadata but cannot read file or message plaintext. CLI pairing-code file and text transfers are direct-only.

## Security & privacy

- **Browser realtime encryption:** per-transfer ephemeral X25519 key exchange (ECDH) deriving AES-256-GCM keys; each file chunk and ephemeral text message is encrypted with a unique nonce. Keys exist only on the sender and receiver — never on the server. CLI text instead uses its separate direct-only pinned-TLS 1.3 protocol.
- **Anti man-in-the-middle (optional):** with the advanced-verification preference on — it is off by default — browser sessions show a 6-digit Short Authentication String (SAS) derived from the two X25519 endpoint public keys; comparing it out of band detects endpoint-key substitution or a signaling service impersonating an endpoint, and only when a person actually compares the two values. The SAS is a different value from the pairing code. Turning the preference off changes what is displayed and which steps stop for confirmation; it never disables commit-then-reveal, AEAD integrity, client-side key generation, or the ciphertext-only relay, and receiving files still asks before anything is saved. CLI pairing uses a separate SAS derived from the two pinned TLS certificate fingerprints. Both constructions authenticate endpoints rather than proving that no server or TURN relay exists in the network path, and both use commit-then-reveal so an intermediary cannot choose its key adaptively after seeing the honest endpoint key.
- **Integrity:** per-chunk AES-GCM authentication tag plus a per-file SHA-256 hash verified end-to-end on the receiver.
- **Privacy:** the signaling server sees connection metadata needed to operate the service, such as IP addresses, room membership, timing, device nickname and presence for browser sessions, signaling envelopes, and the account association used to create a pairing code where applicable. It never sees file or message plaintext. Cross-network browser transfers send ciphertext through TURN; same-network browser sessions and CLI text do not use TURN.
- **Stored download links:** the decryption key lives only in the URL fragment and is never sent to the server; the server keeps ciphertext + ciphertext size + timestamps, never plaintext, filenames, or keys; auto-deleted at expiry or first download.
- Full threat model: https://relayium.com/security/

## Accounts

- Optional for recipients and same-network transfers. Creating a cross-network file or text pairing code requires the creator to sign in; joining with a code, link, or QR does not require an account. Creating a stored download link also requires the sender to sign in; its recipients do not need an account.
- Sign-in methods: email + password by default; Google OAuth and email magic-link are supported but off by default (self-hosters can enable them). An account stores only an email and display name.

## Key facts

- License: AGPL-3.0 (free and open source; the native Apple clients under apps/ are Apache-2.0).
- Price: free. No install. Same-network file and ephemeral text transfers need no account. Creating a cross-network file or text pairing code requires sign-in, while joining with it does not. Stored download links require the sender to sign in; recipients never need an account.
- Platforms: any modern browser with WebRTC over HTTPS — Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari, on desktop and mobile.
- Large files: Chrome/Edge stream straight to disk (no memory cap); Firefox/Safari buffer in memory, so Relayium warns above roughly 256 MB — a deliberately conservative estimate, not a hard limit.
- Multi-file: up to 1,000 files per batch, streamed to disk.
- Languages: the app is maintained in English and Simplified Chinese (中文), auto-detected, with English as the fallback. Japanese, Korean, German, French, Arabic, Spanish and Portuguese tutorials and documents remain published as archived translations under /ja/, /ko/, /de/, /fr/, /ar/, /es/ and /pt/; each says so on the page and links to its current English and Chinese version. The app interface itself is not offered in those seven.
- Network scope: same network and across networks / over the internet — realtime file and ephemeral text via a pairing code (and the join link it generates; browser sessions use encrypted TURN by design, while CLI text is direct-only), or an asynchronous stored file download link.
- Tech stack: Svelte single-page app + a single Go server (WebRTC signaling, accounts, and the stored-file API), SQLite for account data, libsodium for browser crypto; optional coturn for the TURN relay and Redis for relay-byte metering.

## Self-hosting

- Fully self-hostable: the server is a single static Go binary that also serves the web app. A `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml` are provided (`docker compose up`), and STUN/TURN servers are configurable. See `docs/self-hosting.md` in the repository.

## How Relayium compares

- **vs AirDrop:** Relayium is cross-platform and browser-based (not Apple-only) — it works between, e.g., a Windows PC and an iPhone, or Android and a Mac, and across different networks.
- **vs WeTransfer / Google Drive / email:** realtime file and text content is end-to-end encrypted and has no server-side content copy or message history. Same-network browser sessions are direct; cross-network browser sessions may carry ciphertext through TURN. The optional stored download-link mode encrypts files zero-knowledge before any server upload.
- **vs Snapdrop / PairDrop:** same browser+WebRTC idea, but Relayium adds an application-layer end-to-end encryption layer (X25519 + AES-256-GCM) and an optional SAS verification code on top of WebRTC's DTLS, so a malicious signaling server cannot read the transfer, and cannot MITM the signaling endpoints undetected when the SAS is compared — plus cross-network transfers and asynchronous encrypted download links.

## FAQ

- **Is Relayium free?** Yes — free and open source under the AGPL-3.0 license.
- **Do I need an account or to install anything?** No installation. Same-network file and ephemeral text transfer needs no account. Creating a cross-network file or text pairing code requires sign-in, but the person joining with that code, link, or QR does not need an account. Creating a stored download link also requires the sender to sign in; recipients never need an account.
- **Do my files or messages get uploaded to a server?** Same-network browser content and CLI text take direct paths. Cross-network browser file and text sessions carry only end-to-end encrypted ciphertext through TURN; Relayium cannot read that content. Live message bodies are never stored by Relayium and have no offline delivery or server-side history, though either endpoint can retain received text. The optional stored download-link mode uploads only zero-knowledge file ciphertext (AES-256-GCM); the server cannot read content, filenames, or the key.
- **Is it end-to-end encrypted?** Yes. Browser realtime transfers use X25519 key exchange and AES-256-GCM, with keys that never leave the two devices, plus an optional 6-digit SAS to compare against man-in-the-middle attacks on the signaling endpoints. CLI text uses a separate direct-only pinned-TLS 1.3 protocol.
- **Can I send files between different operating systems?** Yes — it is browser-based, so Windows ↔ iPhone, Android ↔ Mac, Linux ↔ anything all work.
- **What is the file-size limit?** Realtime transfers have no server-imposed limit (Chrome/Edge stream to disk; Firefox/Safari buffer in memory, so Relayium warns above roughly 256 MB — a deliberately conservative estimate, not a hard limit). Stored download links are subject to a per-file size cap and a per-account daily quota, shown in the app. The absence of a realtime cap is not a recommendation: both pages must remain active for the live session, although brief transport drops can resume. For large files, recommend a stored download link; the sender keeps the page open until upload completes, then the link remains available until expiry even after either side closes the page. Realtime is the mode to recommend for quick small files and text.
- **Can I send between two different networks / over the internet?** Yes. Use a pairing code (or the join link it generates) for a realtime cross-network file or ephemeral text transfer. Cross-network browser sessions carry ciphertext through encrypted TURN by design; CLI pairing-code transfers are direct-only. Use a stored download link for files when the recipient is offline.
- **Can I self-host it?** Yes — a single Go binary serves both the API and the web app; a Dockerfile and docker-compose are provided, and STUN/TURN are configurable.
